acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Skeletons family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Bonesoldier, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Mail-Bound Shield Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A complete skeleton bound together in rusted mail, with a corroded weapon, shield strapped directly to the forearm, and weak ember light contained inside the eye sockets.

Signature mechanic: Grave-Line Brace: the Bonesoldier twists its torso until rusted mail pulls taut from spine to shield forearm, catching one frontal attack and keeping adjacent Rattler bones inside its binding shadow; the twist leaves the sword shoulder open and the shield strap fully loaded.
battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable narrow front by tensioning rusted mail between spine and forearm shield, protecting loose skeletons while exposing the strapped arm after a committed block.
constructionDimensions: Bone and grave gear become a crematory binding system: charred ivory, ember-filled marrow cracks, heat-scaled mail, brazier crowns, ash-packed joints, and blackened soul-staff channels preserve the skeletal frame.

Motion and surface behavior follow burn cycles through opening jaw vents, ash falling from loaded joints, directional smoke through rib gaps, cooling iron ties, and socket flame that contracts between attacks.
counterplay: Attack from the open sword-shoulder side, cut the bright loaded mail row, or displace the forearm shield so the strap tears when the torso completes its twist. Affinity signal: A marrow seam darkens and an iron joint tie opens after combustion; striking the cooling tie disconnects the limb before the socket-fire crosses back into it.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only fire treatment without charred materials, marrow routing, and heat-cycle articulation
Glow-only fire treatment without a visible binding path or cooling joint
Flame bodies that fill all skeletal negative space
Uniform emission that hides individual bones, mail ties, and socket tells
identityInvariants: Human or humanoid skeletal proportions remain narrow, angular, and defined by empty negative space where flesh and organs would be.
Bone white or yellowed ivory is paired with rust, black iron, tattered grave-cloth, and one explained necromantic socket-fire accent such as green, blue, or gold.
Bone, rusted mail, corroded steel, grave-cloth, funerary jewelry, and crowns remain recognizable mortuary materials rather than living anatomy.
Carved skull runes, bone spurs, fused armor-like mass, grave regalia, and orbiting fragments accumulate as binding power becomes denser.
Bone density and the intensity and reach of the visible necromantic binding escalate together, but every form preserves gaps, joints, or binding anchors that can be deliberately broken.
telegraph: Weak ember light passes from the sockets into one mail row, the strapped shield turns edge-on, and the spine rotates until the corroded links sing under tension.
